proposal.residence_time_basis: Nominal liquid residence time calculated as geometric reactor volume divided by total liquid inlet flow: 10.0 mL / 1.0 mL min-1 = 10.0 min. This is an intended target only and is not executable with the listed inventory because no 50 C thermal-control hardware is available.
proposal.light_setup: None. No light source is listed, and the source batch procedure used microwave irradiation rather than photochemistry.

streams.pump_role: Syringe pump A; single premixed homogeneous feed
streams.contents: DMF solution containing aromatic bromide at 0.100 M, phenylboronic acid derivative, the same base, and the same palladium catalyst/loading used in the validated batch protocol. Exact identities and loadings of boronic acid, base, and catalyst were not supplied and must not be inferred.
streams.phase: single liquid phase only; do not pump a slurry
streams.molar_equiv: Aromatic bromide = 1.0 equivalent; boronic-acid, base, and catalyst equivalents are unspecified in the source protocol and must match the batch record.

proposal.mixer_type: No in-line mixer proposed; one pre-homogenized liquid feed is used because only one pump is listed and no mixer is listed.
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: The batch procedure combines all reagents before heating. A single premixed feed preserves that order and avoids requiring an unlisted second pump, tee, or static mixer. This approach is acceptable only if every component is demonstrably dissolved and remains homogeneous in DMF at the planned feed concentration.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare the feed at 0.100 M in aromatic bromide using DMF and the exact batch catalyst/base/boronic-acid loadings.
Verify visually that the feed is fully homogeneous before loading the syringe; no solids, settling, or gas evolution may be present.
Do not substitute an unlisted filter, mixer, heater, or additional pump under the frozen inventory constraint.

Before operation, obtain documented pressure ratings for the selected 10 mL PFA coil and the selected 5 bar BPR, and provide a qualified temperature-control method capable of holding the entire reactor at exactly 50 C.
post_reactor_steps: Intended configuration after validation: route reactor outlet through a 5 bar BPR and collect the liquid effluent for off-line analysis.
Do not operate or collect pressurized effluent until the BPR pressure rating and downstream containment/collection arrangement are documented.
Analyze steady-state fractions separately; for a 10 min nominal residence time, do not interpret material collected before at least three nominal residence times as steady-state material.
chemistry_notes: The reported 91% batch yield was obtained under 50 W microwave irradiation at 50 C for 10 min. Microwave heating can differ from externally heated flow even at the same nominal bulk temperature.

This is a Suzuki-type coupling description, but the specific aryl bromide, boronic-acid derivative, palladium precursor/ligand, and base are unspecified; no substrate-specific solubility, catalyst-stability, or conversion claim can be made.
Base precipitation or palladium solids could foul 1.0 mm-ID tubing. The single-stream design is conditional on confirmed homogeneous solution behavior.
The 0.100 M aromatic-bromide concentration is an explicitly chosen conservative screen concentration, not a value recovered from the batch report.

stage_parameters.pump: Syringe pump A at 1.00 mL min-1; within its stated 0.01-5.00 mL min-1 range
stage_parameters.run_status: Do not execute with current inventory.

reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: The 10 mL coil is selected because it gives the desired 10 min residence time at a practical 1.00 mL min-1 flow.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No photochemical setup is appropriate because the source specifies microwave irradiation, not a wavelength-dependent light reaction.
reasoning_per_field.streams: One stream is required because the inventory contains one pump only; premixing avoids unlisted mixing hardware.
reasoning_per_field.safety_status: Blocked pending temperature-control availability and documented pressure compatibility.

literature_analogies: General thermal-flow practice commonly translates a batch reaction by matching nominal temperature and residence time, but this is only a screening heuristic and is not evidence that microwave-assisted conversion will transfer unchanged.
No substrate-specific or catalyst-specific literature analogy was supplied or independently verified from the frozen design input.
safety_flags: BLOCK: no listed heater, heating jacket, bath, microwave-flow unit, or other thermal-control device can hold the reactor at exactly 50 C.
BLOCK: pressure ratings for the PFA coils and BPRs are absent; a 5 bar operating pressure cannot be verified against all component limits.
Potential solids/fouling risk in 1.0 mm-ID tubing if the unspecified base, boronic acid, or palladium species is not fully soluble in DMF.
The pump and tubing ratings alone do not validate the full pressurized flow path.
Do not assume microwave and conventional thermal heating are equivalent.

No device capable of heating and maintaining the PFA coil at exactly 50 C is listed. In addition, no pressure rating is provided for either the PFA coil or the available BPRs, so operation at a selected 5 bar back-pressure cannot be verified against all relevant component ratings. The microwave result also does not establish that conventional thermal flow at 50 C will reproduce the reported conversion. The proposal below records an otherwise conservative target condition, but it must not be run until a qualified 50 C temperature-control unit and pressure ratings for the coil and BPR are supplied.
